Markets are trembling amid the latest AI stock sell-off, which has sent shares of major AI players deep into the red. But CNBC's Jim Cramer believes the downturn is not another dot-com crash.

Cramer warned that AI stocks could fall further, particularly semiconductor companies whose shares surged during the AI boom. However, he argued that unlike the speculative businesses that collapsed in 2000, many of today's AI companies are highly profitable.

His biggest concern is smaller AI infrastructure companies such as CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius, which have borrowed heavily to finance data center projects that could face regulatory delays.

Before the election too, Cramer was more careful about tech. On Mad Money, he said the Nasdaq had just closed its worst month since March 2025 and that the week ahead "might be even worse." He said he wanted to see a "crescendo" before putting more money into tech, which he described as stocks getting crushed in the morning and then rallying on big volume to finish higher. He also warned that anti-data center politicians could stop projects if Democrats took control, and data center stocks fell on Wednesday on fears of tighter AI regulation, Reuters reported.

We recently ranked 10 stocks Cramer sounded positive about, based on his posts on X and his comments on CNBC. Click to see the full list of 10 stocks Cramer likes here.

Methodology

For this article, we scanned Jim Cramer's X feed and watched his latest Mad Money programs on CNBC to pick 10 stocks he sounded positive about. We ranked them in ascending order by the number of hedge fund holders at the end of the second quarter of 2026, according to Insider Monkey's database of 1,006 hedge funds.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. #5 GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE:GEV)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 106

GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) makes gas turbines, wind turbines, and equipment for power grids. On X on Oct. 28, Cramer called the stock "an opportunity." In another post that day, he wrote that he was trying "to get into the brains of the GE Vernova sellers," and joked that he was not sure they had any. He sees the selling as a mistake. GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) is one of the names he is watching closely. Barometer Capital Management pointed to the company's gas turbine and grid backlog in its second-quarter 2026 investor letter. IREN has seen its share price swing sharply in recent years, which puts fresh focus on a simple question for you as an investor. Does the current US$18.03 price make sense relative to the sales the business is generating today and what those sales could reasonably support over time?

Over the past 3 years the stock has delivered a very large gain of about 7x, which now puts a lot of weight on whether its sales base can carry that kind of move.

Recent contract delays with Microsoft and a sizeable capital spending plan can reshape both the timing of future revenue and the funding required, which feeds directly into how much sales investors may be willing to pay for right now.

There is a second opinion on IREN worth weighing. See what analysts think IREN's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether IREN's current market value is justified by its sales once you compare it with the Fair Ratio benchmark.

If you want a second reference point alongside IREN's recent swings and contract headlines, you can look at a focused screen of 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Is IREN a Bargain on Sales?

Price to sales suits IREN because the business is still reporting losses, so the market is mostly anchoring on revenue rather than earnings. At roughly 10.0x P/S, the stock trades above the wider Software sector average of about 3.5x but below the more focused peer group near 15.2x, which places it in the middle of a very growth‑heavy cluster of AI infrastructure plays.

The Fair Ratio, which reflects what investors might typically pay for IREN given its growth profile, margins, size and risk mix, sits above the current P/S, so the shares screen as undervalued on this framework. Despite the Microsoft contract delays and capex questions that have unsettled AI data center stocks during 2026, the present multiple still prices IREN at a discount to what this model suggests could be justified for its sales base. title: IREN CEO: Old Nvidia H100s Just Recontracted at “Double the Original Contract Price”
detail:
IREN CEO: Old Nvidia H100s Just Recontracted at “Double the Original Contract Price”
Roxanna Maglangit

IREN
NVDA
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
IREN CEO: Old Nvidia H100s Just Recontracted at "Double the Original Contract Price" ©@Handmadefont from Handmadefont via Canva
Key Takeaways

IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts said on the company's Nov. 5 earnings call that older NVIDIA H100 GPUs were just recontracted at double their original contract price.

Old chips earning more on a second contract supports IREN's revenue and the useful life of NVIDIA's installed base.

IREN's capital spending reached $4.82 billion in the September 2026 quarter, and short seller Jim Chanos argues its capital base is too big for its revenue.

A new contract with a customer prepaying about 90% of the GPU capex answers part of that worry, and IREN traded at 3.1x forward sales on Nov. 2, below its three-year average of 5.2x.

IREN (IREN:NASDAQ) went into its Nov. 5 report after a roughly 20% slide, on news from The Information that delays at its Childress, Texas site held up some of Microsoft's AI spending.

Then co-founder and co-CEO Daniel Roberts gave NVIDIA (NVDA:NASDAQ) shareholders a line worth hearing on IREN's fiscal first-quarter call:

"Older generation H100s, we just recontracted at double the original contract price."

Which is a remarkable thing to say about hardware that old.

And IREN isn't the only one seeing it. As Dave Blundin put it on this week's episode of Moonshots with Peter Diamandis: "we're seeing H100 prices increasing, which is insane, on chips that are how old? Three years old now."

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on IREN, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See IREN's Analyst Ratings

Old chips that still earn

The worry about GPU clouds has been that the chips lose their value before they pay off. IREN's own math on its Microsoft contract assumed its GPUs would be worth nothing after five years.

If a three-year-old H100 can rent for twice its first contract, that assumption looks conservative. That's good news for IREN, which keeps each GPU when a contract ends. It's good news for NVIDIA too, since its chips are still earning money for its customers years after they shipped.

IREN's newest deals point the same way. In the days before the call, it signed a five-year contract at about $22 million of annualized revenue per megawatt and a shorter one at more than $40 million, Roberts said. A leading frontier AI lab also expanded its capacity with IREN again.

Analysts already expected IREN's revenue to roughly quadruple, from $707 million in fiscal 2026 to $2.81 billion in fiscal 2027 (the year ending June 2027), then reach $7.41 billion the year after.
